newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TUGNUTT POSTS SECOND CONSECUTIVE SHUTOUT IN OTTAWA WIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TUGNUTT POSTS SECOND CONSECUTIVE SHUTOUT IN OTTAWA WIN.

text.p: After going more than three years without a shutout, Ottawa Senators goaltender Ron Tugnutt blanked the Washington Capitals on Thursday for his second shutout in as many days.
Tugnutt, who blanked Buffalo 2-0 Wednesday, stopped 25 shots and Lance Pitlick had a goal and an assist as the Senators downed the Capitals 4-0 for their franchise-record fourth straight victory.
"I feel very confident, the guys are playing very well in front of me," said Tugnutt, who has allowed just four goals in his last four starts. "I'm enjoying the ice time."

Alexandre Daigle, Tom Chorske and Alexei Yashin also scored for Ottawa, which solidified its hold on the club's first ever playoff berth, moving within one point of seventh-place Montreal in the Eastern Conference.

Daigle's 26th goal with 70 seconds left in the first period gave Tugnutt all the support he needed. Yashin completed the scoring with his 34th goal as Washington fell three points behind the Senators for the final playoff spot.
In Pittsburgh, the Penguins clinched a playoff berth but were denied a victory when Keith Primeau's second goal of the game with 3:37 left lifted the Hartford Whalers to a 5-5 tie.
Jaromir Jagr scored his 47th goal and set up two for the Penguins, who are two points back of the fifth-place Rangers.
The Penguins rallied from a goal down in the third as Jagr set up Mario Lemieux's 48th goal at 5:28 and Ron Francis's 26th to put Pittsburgh in front with 7:34 remaining.
Lemieux's 611th career goal moved him ahead of the great Bobby Hull into sole possession of sixth place on the NHL all-time goals list.
In New York, Mark Messier had a goal and two assists as the Rangers broke out to a 5-1 lead and hung on for a 5-4 victory over the Boston Bruins to clinch a playoff berth.

Defenceman Jeff Beukeboom had a goal and an assist in a four-goal first period for the Rangers, who strengthened their hold on fifth place in the East and crept within two points of the fourth-place Florida Panthers.
Wayne Gretzky, Adam Graves and David Oliver also scored for New York, which halted a four-game winless streak (0-2-1).
Landon Wilson had two goals and an assist for Boston, which scored the game's last three goals.
In Detroit, Brendan Shanahan and Tim Taylor scored third-period goals to rally the Red Wings to a 2-2 tie with the Toronto Maple Leafs.
The Red Wings, who have gone into overtime in each of their last five games, clinched third place in the Western Conference behind Colorado and Dallas.

Toronto carried a 2-0 lead into the third period on goals by Nick Kypreos and Dimitri Yushkevich. Shanahan's team-best 47th goal at 2:39 drew Detroit within one. Taylor beat Felix Potvin to tie the game at 10:50 of the third.
Potvin finished with 34 saves while Chris Osgood stopped 28 shots for Detroit.
In St Louis, Zigmund Palffy's second goal of the game with 1:54 left in regulation capped a three-goal comeback as the New York Islanders rallied for a 5-5 tie with the Blues.

The Blues appeared to have taken a 6-4 lead at 17:59, but Craig Conroy's goal was disallowed when replays showed him to be in the crease. Palffy tied the game with his 47th goal of the season just seven seconds later, beating Grant Fuhr between the pads with a wrist shot from the faceoff circle.

Geoff Courtnall and Pavol Demitra scored 33 seconds apart in the third to give St Louis a 5-2. But Travis Green and Todd Bertuzzi pulled the Isles within one, setting the stage for Palffy, who also scored the game's first goal.
In Edmonton, Mike Grier's powerplay goal with 6:57 left in the third period snapped a tie as the Oilers skated to a 4-2 victory over the Chicago Blackhawks.

Mariusz Czerkawksi's shot was stopped by goaltender Jeff Hackett, but Grier banged in the rebound from the left doorstep for a 3-2 lead. Kelly Buchberger added an empty netter with eight seconds left to complete the scoring.
Bryan Marchment and Ryan Smyth also scored for Edmonton, which moved into a fifth-place tie with Anaheim in the West.
Curtis Joseph made 32 saves, allowing goals by Chicago's Bob Probert and Sergei Krivokrasov.
In Los Angeles, Keith Tkachuk had a pair of goals and an assist and Teppo Numminen snapped a 3-3 second-period as the Phoenix Coyotes beat the Kings 5-4.
After Numminen put Phoenix in front 4-3 with just over five minutes left in the second, Coyotes goaltender Nikolai Khabibulin stonewalled the Kings over the next 24 minutes.
Tkachuk's empty-net goal -- his 49th of the season -- with 46 seconds left put Phoenix ahead 5-3 before Khabibulin gave up a goal by Brad Smyth with four seconds to play.
The win leaves the Coyotes alone in fourth place in the West, one point ahead of Anaheim and Edmonton.
